newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade strained, rates firm.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade strained, rates firm.

text.p: The Croatian money market trade remained strained on Monday with firm interest rates as supply fell short of demand again after days of crisis, dealers said.
"Term funds are in particularly short supply but borrowers have been settling for call money loans in their absence," one money dealer told Reuters.
Call money and two-day rates were steady at 10.5 percent, with savings banks charging one another 12 percent. The 15-day interbank rate was also unchanged at 13 percent.
The morning trade was put at a high 45.6 million kuna against demand for over 50 million, despite last week's interventions by the central bank to boost liquidity.
This situation, caused by large payouts by banks' clients, was seen as exacerbating further by Wednesday, when they must repay 190 million kuna in repo funds taken out last Friday.
But the central bank said it planned no other steps at this stage to help the banking sector further. It had also purchased hard currency from it last week to increase money supply.

Overall banks' balances ended at 332 million kuna at the week-end after sinking to 226 million before the interventions. Banks bought some 45 million kuna overnight funds to get by. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
